title: Vietnamese Beef Phở
description: Traditional beef noodle soup with a rich, clear bone broth.

steps.instruction_text: Roast the spices and simmer the beef bones for 6–8 hours to create the broth.
Blanch the rice noodles and place them in a bowl.

title: Bún Bò Huế
description: A spicy, deeply aromatic central Vietnamese beef and pork noodle soup infused with lemongrass and shrimp paste.

steps.instruction_text: Parboil and rinse the beef bones, pork hocks, and beef shank to remove impurities before beginning the main clear broth.
Simmer the rinsed bones and meats in fresh water alongside bruised lemongrass stalks for 2 to 3 hours, skimming the surface regularly.
Dissolve the mắm ruốc shrimp paste in cold water, let the solids settle, then ladle the clear seasoned liquid into the simmering broth.
Heat oil in a small pan, fry the annatto seeds until the oil turns a deep vibrant red, strain out the seeds, and pour the colored oil into the soup broth.
Boil the thick round rice noodles until tender, drain, and assemble in serving bowls topped with sliced meats, hot broth, and fresh herbs.

title: Bún Chả Hà Nội
description: Hanoi-style smoky charcoal-grilled pork patties and pork belly served swimming in a warm, sweet-tangy dipping broth with light vermicelli noodles.

steps.instruction_text: Marinate the ground pork shoulder and sliced pork belly in separate bowls using minced garlic, shallots, fish sauce, and nước màu for at least 1 hour.
Shape the ground pork into flat round patties, then grill both the patties and the pork belly slices over charcoal until beautifully charred and cooked through.
Thinly slice the green papaya, massage with salt, rinse, and quick-pickle them in sugar and vinegar for 20 minutes to maintain crispiness.
Simmer fish sauce, sugar, vinegar, and water to build a warm, diluted dipping broth; stir in the pickled papaya chunks along with fresh chili.
Serve the warm broth filled with grilled pork meats on a large platter next to plates of fresh rice vermicelli and clean perilla herbs.

title: Bánh Xèo
description: Crispy, sizzling yellow rice flour pancakes filled with pork belly strips, fresh shrimp, and bean sprouts.

steps.instruction_text: Whisk together rice flour, turmeric powder, salt, coconut milk, and water until completely smooth, then stir in the sliced green onions and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat a drop of oil in a hot skillet, sear a few pieces of pork belly and shrimp for 1 minute until partially cooked.
Ladle a thin layer of batter into the pan, swirling rapidly to coat the entire cooking surface until thin and sizzling.
Place a handful of raw bean sprouts on one side of the crepe, cover with a lid for 2 minutes to steam the sprouts, then cook uncovered until the edges turn golden and crispy.
Fold the pancake cleanly in half over the fillings and slide onto a platter to be cut up and wrapped inside mustard green leaves with herbs.

title: Bánh Bèo
description: Central Vietnamese steamed savory rice cakes served in small ceramic saucers, topped with dried shrimp flakes, crispy pork rinds, and scallion oil.

steps.instruction_text: Whisk rice flour, tapioca starch, salt, cold water, and a splash of boiling water into a smooth, thin batter, then let it rest for 30 minutes.
Boil, finely mince, and dehydrate the fresh shrimp in a dry skillet over low heat until they turn into fluffy, vibrant orange shrimp flakes.
Fry the diced pork skin in deep oil until puffed and crunchy to create crispy pork rinds.
Heat melted lard in a pan and pour it directly over sliced green onions in a bowl to create aromatic scallion oil.

Steam empty small ceramic saucers in a hot steamer, ladle a thin layer of batter into each cup, cover for 5 minutes until translucent, then top with scallion oil, shrimp flakes, pork rinds, and sweet fish sauce.

title: Hủ Tiếu Nam Vang
description: A popular Cambodian-Chinese-Vietnamese hybrid noodle soup featuring chewy clear tapioca noodles, pork broth, minced meat, pork slices, liver, and quail eggs.

steps.instruction_text: Simmer parboiled pork tubular bones along with toasted dried shrimp and squid for 2 hours, skimming constantly to keep the broth perfectly clear.
Sauté the ground pork in a pan with minced garlic and seasoning until fully cooked and crumbly.
Poach the pork loin slices and pork liver slices directly in the hot bone broth until cooked through, then remove and plunge into cold water to prevent darkening.
Quickly blanch the chewy tapioca hủ tiếu noodles in boiling water, shake dry, and toss immediately with fried garlic oil in a serving bowl to prevent sticking.
Assemble the serving bowls by arranging pork slices, cooked ground pork, liver, quail eggs, and fresh Chinese chives over the noodles before ladling the scalding hot broth on top.

title: Bún Riêu Cua
description: A comforting freshwater crab tomato noodle soup topped with airy crab-egg soufflé patties, fried tofu, and congealed pork blood blocks.

steps.instruction_text: Simmer the pork ribs for 1.5 hours to extract a sweet, clear base broth.
Whisk minced paddy crab meat with eggs and a touch of shrimp paste, then ladle gently into simmering broth until the protein floats up into cloud-like soufflé rafts.
Sauté the tomato wedges until softened and add them to the soup along with fried tofu puffs to infuse color and tanginess.
Ladle the vibrant red broth and floating crab egg cakes over fresh bowls of thin rice vermicelli noodles.

title: Mì Quảng
description: Central Vietnamese flat turmeric rice noodles served with a highly concentrated shallow broth, pork, shrimp, crushed peanuts, and toasted rice crackers.

steps.instruction_text: Sauté crushed cu nen chives in vibrant red annatto oil until exceptionally fragrant.
Toss the pork belly and shrimp into the oil, browning rapidly with heavy seasoning to yield a rich, highly concentrated shallow sauce base.

Layer wide turmeric rice noodles into a serving dish, ladle just enough intense broth to partially wet the noodles, then garnish heavily with crushed roasted peanuts and broken crunchy sesame rice crackers.

title: Cao Lầu
description: An exclusive, historic noodle dish from Hội An featuring thick, springy wood-ash clarified noodles, sweet char siu style pork, and crunchy fried square crackers.

steps.instruction_text: Marinate the entire pork loin block heavily in five-spice powder, soy sauce, garlic, and sugar for 2 hours.
Braise the pork in a pan until deeply caramelized, reserving the rich bottom pan glaze to act as your thick noodle dressing.
Steam your unique, springy ash-water lye rice noodles, slice the braised pork thinly, and arrange them together over local wild greens before adding fried square dough croutons.

title: Bánh Canh Hẹ
description: A specialty thick tapioca noodle soup from Phú Yên completely blanketed in finely chopped fresh green chives and tender local fish cakes.

ingredients.name: Fried Vietnamese fish cake sheets (Chả Cá)

steps.instruction_text: Simmer clean mackerel bones for 1 hour to yield a light, sweet seafood broth base.
Blanch thick tapioca noodles and place them into bowls alongside boiled quail eggs and sliced strips of fried fish cake.
ingredients_used: Fried Vietnamese fish cake sheets (Chả Cá)

steps.instruction_text: Completely blanket the top surface of the bowl with a thick, dense layer of finely minced fresh green chives, then ladle scalding hot fish broth right over the herbs to flash-cook them.

title: Bánh Canh Trảng Bàng
description: A legendary clean, clear pork noodle soup from Tây Ninh showcasing dew-moistened thick flour noodles and tender boiled pork leg slices.

steps.instruction_text: Simmer the entire pork leg thigh section slowly with toasted shallots and black peppercorns to create a crystal-clear pork essence broth.
Remove the tender pork leg, plunge it into cold water to preserve texture, and cut into neat, thin discs.
Submerge your Trảng Bàng rice noodles in boiling water, drain, top with the sliced boiled pork meat, cover with broth, and serve instantly alongside an assorted wild herb platter.

title: Hủ Tiếu Mỹ Tho
description: Southern Vietnamese noodle dish utilizing distinctively chewy, sun-dried clear glass noodles tossed in sweet soy reduction glaze.

steps.instruction_text: Blanch the clear, chewy sun-dried Mỹ Tho noodles and quickly coat them with your prepared oyster sauce soy reduction.
Top the glossy noodles with hot sautéed minced pork, peeled boiled shrimp, and a generous sprinkle of crispy fried pork lardons.

title: Cơm Tấm
description: Vibrant broken rice grain platter served with a sweet lemongrass-marinated grilled pork chop, egg-meat loaf, and sweet fish sauce dressing.

steps.instruction_text: Steam the broken rice grains gently until perfectly fluffy yet distinct in texture.
Grill the lemongrass pork chops over a screaming hot griddle until deeply caramelized on the edges.
Mound the warm broken rice on a flat plate, lay down your grilled cutlets, add a slice of egg meat loaf, and drizzle with scallion oil oil garnish and sweet fish sauce.

title: Cơm Lam
description: Sticky fragrant mountain rice packed densely and slow-roasted inside fresh bamboo segments over hot glowing coals.

steps.instruction_text: Soak your fragrant sticky rice in water for 6 hours, then pack it snugly inside the fresh green bamboo tubes, adding a touch of water.
Plug the tube open ends firmly using rolled banana leaves, then roast over hot coals, rotating regularly for 1 hour until the bamboo outer husk burns down black.
Peel away the charred bamboo layers to expose the clean internal rice log, slice into rounds, and serve with toasted peanut sesame salt.

title: Cơm Hến
description: A crisp, complex room-temperature rice bowl from Huế filled with tiny stir-fried baby clams, crunch pork skin rinds, and warm clam broth on the side.

steps.instruction_text: Boil baby marsh clams to clean them, keeping the residual pot water as your seasoned warm side broth.
Stir-fry the shucked clam flesh rapidly with minced garlic and a touch of intense Huế shrimp paste.
Assemble by scattering the sautéed clams over bowls of cool cooked rice, adding crunchy puffy pork rinds, shredded banana flower blossoms, and serving the warm broth on the side.

title: Gỏi Cuốn
description: Healthy translucent fresh summer rice paper rolls wrapping fresh shrimp, lean pork slices, vermicelli, and crisp garlic chive stems.

steps.instruction_text: Lightly moisten a rice paper sheet until pliable, then layer down crisp lettuce, herbs, and a small bundle of rice vermicelli lines.
Place boiled pork shoulder slices followed by the split shrimp halves skin-side down on the paper boundary.
Tuck the sides in firmly, roll halfway, drop in a whole garlic chive stem so it protrudes outward, and roll completely shut; serve alongside hoisin peanut dipping sauce.

title: Chả Giò
description: Crispy fried golden egg rolls loaded with minced pork, wood-ear mushrooms, shredded taro, and glass cellphane noodles.

steps.instruction_text: Thoroughly knead the minced pork together with chopped wood-ear mushrooms, shredded taro, and soaked cut glass cellophane noodles.
Enclose small portions of your meat filling tightly inside deep-fry spring roll wrappers, pasting the tips down securely.
Submerge the rolls inside bubbling frying oil over medium heat, cooking until the skins crisp up into a rich golden brown.

title: Bánh Tét
description: A dense Lunar New Year cylindrical sticky rice log packed with pork belly and yellow mung bean paste, wrapped tightly in banana leaves.

steps.instruction_text: Flatten out a dense layer of glutinous sweet rice over clean banana leaf sheets, layer mashed cooked mung beans down the spine, and top with seasoned pork belly strips.
Roll the leaf tightly into a uniform cylinder, fold down the open ends neatly, and secure structural stability using multiple butcher string ties wrapped horizontally.
Submerge your wrapped log completely inside a large stockpot of boiling water, boiling continuously for 8 hours.

title: Bánh Cuốn
description: Delicate, silk-thin steamed fermented rice sheets filled with savory minced pork and wood-ear mushrooms, brushed with scallion oil.

steps.instruction_text: Stir-fry ground pork mix and chopped wood-ear mushrooms together in a pan until thoroughly cooked through.
Ladle a thin layer of fermented rice flour blend onto a taut fabric steamer screen cloth, cover with a lid for 45 seconds to steam into a delicate sheet.
Lift the delicate translucent sheet off using a bamboo stick, drop in your cooked pork filling, roll into a log, and serve garnished with crispy fried shallots and chả lụa slices.

title: Bánh Khọt
description: Miniature crispy savory coconut rice pancakes cooked in a special dimpled cast-iron tray, topped with single whole shrimps and green scallion cream.

steps.instruction_text: Whisk rice flour pancake mix with thick coconut cream and water until it reaches a smooth, pourable pouring thickness.
Oil the dimpled pockets of a hot cast-iron tray, pour batter into each slot, and drop a spoonful of mung bean paste and a small deveined shrimp in the center of each mini-crepe.
Cover with a lid for 3 minutes, then cook uncovered until the shell edges turn crunch-golden; slide out and gloss over with scallion oil grease.

title: Lẩu Mắm
description: An intense, deeply savory Southern fermented mud fish hotpot packed with seafood, pork belly, eggplant cubes, and assorted river wild flowers.

ingredients.name: Fermented mud fish paste (Mắm Cá Linh)

steps.instruction_text: Boil fermented mud fish paste in water until the fish flesh completely dissolves, then strain the broth carefully through a fine sieve to remove bones.
ingredients_used: Fermented mud fish paste (Mắm Cá Linh)

steps.instruction_text: Simmer the strained pungent broth alongside bruised lemongrass stalks, pork belly cubes, and eggplant cubes for 30 minutes.
ingredients_used: Fermented mud fish paste (Mắm Cá Linh)

steps.instruction_text: Transfer the boiling soup to a tabletop hotpot collar, cooking your fresh squid & shrimp platter and wild river flowers on the fly as you dine.

title: Bánh Tráng Cuốn Thịt Heo
description: A popular wrapper dish featuring premium boiled pork belly strips with double-ended fat layers, hand-wrapped in paper with dense wild greens.

steps.instruction_text: Gently simmer the double-fat pork belly strip until cooked through, maintaining clear translucent properties for the fat layers, then slice into long ribbons.
Prepare your intense mắm nêm sauce by tempering pungent anchovy dipping sauce with crushed pineapple, lime juice, chili, and sugar.
Lay a dry rice paper sheet flat, stack assorted herbs, green mango & cucumber matches, and a ribbon of pork belly before rolling cleanly to dip into the mắm nêm.

title: Bún Sứa Nha Trang
description: A crisp, refreshing coastal noodle soup from Nha Trang featuring crunchy jellyfish, savory sailfish cakes, and a light, clear broth simmered from fresh scad or ponyfish.

ingredients.name: Nha Trang fried fish cakes (Chả Cá)

steps.instruction_text: Slowly simmer the fresh scad or ponyfish bones in water for 1.5 hours, skimming frequently to extract a sweet, completely clear coastal fish broth.
Sauté the Roma tomatoes until slightly softened and stir them into the clear fish broth along with a hint of mắm tôm for subtle depth.
Blanch the rice vermicelli noodles and arrange them neatly in bowls, adding sliced rows of fried fish cakes and a handful of raw herbs & cabbage mix.
ingredients_used: Nha Trang fried fish cakes (Chả Cá)

steps.instruction_text: Top the bowls with your crunchy fresh jellyfish slices, ladle the boiling tomato fish broth on top, and serve immediately with fresh chili.

title: Bánh Tráng Trộn
description: The quintessential Southern Vietnamese street food snack: shredded rice paper strips mixed with green mango, jerky, hard-boiled eggs, and a tangy kumquat shallot oil dressing.

steps.instruction_text: Combine the shredded rice paper strips, shredded green mango, beef jerky, and dried shrimp in a large mixing bowl.
Drizzle the aromatic shallot oil and fresh kumquat juice over the ingredients, tossing quickly and gently to soften the rice paper without making it mushy.
Add chopped Vietnamese coriander and the boiled quail eggs, give it one final quick toss, and transfer to a serving container to enjoy instantly.
